title: Derived open/closed site mates retain sheaf restriction normalization
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite discrete commutative ring. Use ordinary derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_W=\nu_W^*$ for the exact etale/pro-etale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. For an open immersion $j$ [def-weil-open-immersion], let $o_j:C_Xj_{e,!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{p,!}C_U$ be the termwise canonical open comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], using extensions by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero], and let $a_j:C_Uj_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_p^*C_X$ be the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For a closed immersion $h:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], let $\delta_h:C_XRh_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{p,*}C_Z$ on $D^+$ be the specified counit-mate comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], and let $a_h:C_Zh_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_p^*C_X$ be canonical pullback comparison. Subscripts $e,p$ mean etale and pro-etale. Composition is read right to left.

Let $X$ be Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]). For every open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, the termwise $a_j,o_j$ on unbounded derived categories respect the derived open units $\eta_j^e,\eta_j^p$ and counits $e_j^e,e_j^p$:
$$j_p^*(o_{j,L})a_{j,j_{e,!}L}C_U(\eta^e_{j,L})=\eta^p_{j,C_UL},\qquad e^p_{j,C_XM}j_{p,!}(a_{j,M})o_{j,j_e^*M}=C_X(e^e_{j,M})$$
for all $L\in D(U_e,A)$ and $M\in D(X_e,A)$.

For every closed immersion $h:Z\hookrightarrow X$, both $h_{e,*}$ and $h_{p,*}$ are exact. Let $\delta_h^0:C_Xh_{e,*}\to h_{p,*}C_Z$ on sheaves be the $h_p^*\dashv h_{p,*}$ transpose of $C_Z(\varepsilon^e_{h,L})a_{h,h_{e,*}L}^{-1}$, where $\varepsilon_h^\tau$ denotes the ordinary closed restriction/direct-image counit. Its termwise descent on $D^+$ is exactly $\delta_h$, under the exact-functor identifications $Rh_{\tau,*}=h_{\tau,*}$. Thus
$$\varepsilon^p_{h,C_ZL}h_p^*(\delta_{h,L})a_{h,h_{e,*}L}=C_Z(\varepsilon^e_{h,L})$$
for $L\in D^+(Z_e,A)$. The closed counits in this equation are invertible. Under them the restriction of $\delta_h$ is the identity of $C_ZL$; under the open units the restriction of $o_j$ is likewise the identity. These equalities use the canonical pullback comparisons, including their composition identifications.

proof.text: All inverse images here are exact on constant-$A$ modules: use [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] for $C_T$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] for etale restriction, and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] with [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] for pro-etale restriction. The latter definition identifies the module pullback with exact abelian inverse image when the coefficient map is invertible. Both open extensions are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], all edges in the open comparison squares preserve quasi-isomorphisms and descend canonically. Their termwise localization is the functor intended in the statement, with its canonical exact-composition identifications; in particular this applies on unbounded complexes.

proof.text:
First work on sheaves, writing $E=j_{e,!}$, $r=j_e^*$, $J=j_{p,!}$, $s=j_p^*$ and $o=o_j$. The comparison $o$ is the canonical one, so [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization] gives
$$s(o_F)a_{EF}C_U(\eta^e_F)=\eta^p_{C_UF}.$$
The $a$ in that node is precisely the canonical pullback comparison of the statement, not an independently chosen identification. This is the required open unit equation before localization.

proof.text:
Derive the sheaf counit equation explicitly. The open adjunctions are [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Put
$$y=C_X(e^e_M)o_{rM}^{-1}:JC_UrM\longrightarrow C_XM.$$
Its $J\dashv s$ transpose, using the preceding unit equation at $F=rM$, is
$$s(y)\eta^p_{C_UrM}=s(C_Xe^e_M)a_{ErM}C_U(\eta^e_{rM})
=a_M C_U(r(e^e_M)\eta^e_{rM})=a_M.$$
The middle equality is naturality of $a$; the last is the etale triangle identity. The inverse-transpose formula therefore gives $y=e^p_{C_XM}J(a_M)$. Compose with $o_{rM}$ on the right to obtain exactly the asserted counit equation on sheaves.

proof.text: Use [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] for the exact open adjunctions: their derived units and counits are the localized termwise sheaf units and counits. Apply [lem-sp-exact-derived-transformation-pasting] to the two sheaf equalities of Steps 2 and 3, with the exact functors of Step 1. Its cells need not be invertible, so it applies to units and counits as well as to $a,o$. It gives both displayed open equations, for all unbounded $L,M$, with exactly the specified termwise $a_j,o_j$ and their canonical composition identifications.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; localization of adjunction transformations and their finite pasting equations

proof.text: The etale open unit is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso]. This abelian-sheaf statement applies to the underlying abelian sheaves of constant-$A$ modules: the extension presheaf and its adjunction maps are the same after forgetting the $A$-action [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. An inverse to an $A$-linear bijection is $A$-linear, since $f(ax)=af(x)$ implies $f^{-1}(ay)=af^{-1}(y)$. The termwise inverse is a chain map by naturality, and localizes to the inverse derived unit. The open unit equation of Step 4, whose other factors are invertible, also makes the pro-etale unit at $C_UL$ invertible. It says precisely that $j_p^*(o_{j,L})$, identified on its source by $a_{j,j_{e,!}L}$ and these units, is the identity of $C_UL$.

source.place: Tag 0F70, lemma-jshriek-open; module version is the same canonical map with its coefficient action

proof.text: For a closed $h:Z\hookrightarrow X$, its complementary open immersion $v$ is quasi-compact. Indeed, for every quasi-compact open $V\subset X$, the inverse image $V\cap(X\setminus Z)$ is an open subscheme of the Noetherian scheme $X$, hence is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Apply [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] to obtain exactness of $h_{p,*}$; the quasi-compactness just checked is its essential hypothesis. On the etale site [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization] identifies $Z_e$ with the closed complement and states exactness and invertibility of the module counit for its direct image. Thus $h_{e,*}$ is exact too. The pro-etale sheaf counit is invertible by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful]. These facts concern all constant-$A$ module sheaves, without constructibility assumptions. Also $h$ is separated and universally closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-quasi-compact] and quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. This verifies the hypotheses of the named direct-image mate comparison used in Step 8.

source.place: Tag 09BM, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact; Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion; etale closed complement: Tag 04CA and sites-modules.tex Tag 08M3

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], the right derived functors of the two now-exact closed direct images are their termwise localizations, with the canonical universal derived comparisons. Their derived adjunctions agree, under these comparisons, with [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. To check the normalization, use the canonical Hom formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] for $F=h_{\tau,*}$ and $G=h_\tau^*$. Both are exact. Every quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to I$ is sent to an isomorphism, so $QF(s)^{-1}$ gives the representing cocone for $RF(K)=QF(K)$; likewise $QG(t)^{-1}$ gives the representing cone for $LG(M)=QG(M)$. These diagrams are isomorphic to constant diagrams, verifying essential constancy. For $s=t=1$, the cited formula identifies the transpose of $Qf$ with $Q(f^\sharp)$; for all other fraction representatives it is the same formula with the inverse images of $s,t$ inserted. The localized ordinary adjunction has this formula too, so uniqueness in that node identifies the Hom bijections. Consequently the canonical derived closed counits are precisely the localized ordinary counits, rather than counits of arbitrarily chosen isomorphic adjunctions.

proof.text:
On sheaves, the defining transpose formula for $\delta_h^0$ gives
$$\varepsilon^p_{h,C_ZF}h_p^*(\delta^0_{h,F})a_{h,h_{e,*}F}=C_Z(\varepsilon^e_{h,F});$$
this is the inverse-transpose identity of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. All functors in this equality are exact by Steps 1 and 6. Therefore [lem-sp-exact-derived-transformation-pasting], together with the counit identification of Step 7, gives the same equation on $D^+$ for the termwise descent $D(\delta_h^0)$. On the other hand [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] defines $\delta_h$ as the transpose of $C_Z(\varepsilon^e_h)a_h^{-1}$ and supplies the same equation. Both maps therefore have the same transpose under $h_p^*\dashv Rh_{p,*}$, so the bijectivity in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives $D(\delta_h^0)=\delta_h$. The closed-immersion instance of the named comparison is exactly the one fixed in the statement; its isomorphism assertion now also shows that this particular localized mate is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; derived.tex Tag 015F for passage of the sheaf transpose equation to exact derived functors

proof.text:
The closed sheaf counits in Step 6 are natural isomorphisms. Their termwise inverses are chain maps and remain inverse after localization, so Step 7 makes both closed derived counits invertible. The equation of Step 8 consequently reads
$$\varepsilon^p_{h,C_ZL}\,h_p^*(\delta_{h,L})\,a_{h,h_{e,*}L}\,(C_Z\varepsilon^e_{h,L})^{-1}=1_{C_ZL},$$
which is exactly the stated closed restriction normalization. The analogous open normalization was proved in Step 5. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] supplies identity and composite compatibility of the canonical sheaf pullback comparisons. [lem-sp-exact-derived-transformation-pasting] carries those equations with their compositors to the derived comparisons. Thus all restrictions above use the canonical composition identifications as asserted, including identity and empty immersions.
